dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation

evidence.note: Exhaustive reading of every skeleton source file, working around terminal truncation with sed/python to fully map Instr/NumOp/MemOp enums, the Value model, and instruction dispatch.
Explicit inventory of stubbed vs buggy items (v128 accessors return 0, missing 0xFD, exec_numeric/Call/CallIndirect stubs, no SimdOp enum) — an explicit codebase map matching the level-8 anchor.
Repeatedly restored original files to preserve compilation and the frozen public API surface; concretely verified which items must not change (spec.rs instantiate signature, field names).

Used wabt wasm-objdump on actual test binaries to confirm 0xFD sub-opcode encoding, discovering v128.const=0x0C and correcting a previously invented opcode table — the level-10 'confirm against wabt-generated output' behavior.

Semantics (saturation, mem_addrs-with-no-memory, arithmetic correctness) discovered reactively through test failures rather than pinned from spec upfront, capping the semantic-research aspect below the full level-8 clause.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built an explicit, accurate map of the skeleton (stubs, bugs, frozen public contract, value/stack model), matching the level-8 codebase-orientation clause, and performed genuine encoding re-research against wabt-generated disassembly with sustained probing of specific spec-test cases (a level-10 signal). However, it initially invented opcode numbers and discovered per-family semantics (saturation, lane order, NaN) reactively through failures rather than pinning them down from the spec, so it falls short of level 8's proactive-semantics requirement. This lands it at 7 — strong codebase orientation and real encoding verification, weaker proactive semantic research.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones

evidence.note: Early explicit decomposition with dependency ordering: types.rs (add SimdOp/V128Const) → decode.rs (0xFD prefix) → runtime.rs (v128 lane accessors) → exec_numeric/Call, then full SIMD. MVP fixes sequenced alongside SIMD scaffolding — more than a vague two-phase idea.

Repeatedly enumerates the full SIMD family surface (i8x16, i16x8, i32x4, i64x2, f32x4, f64x2 arithmetic, narrowing, widening, extmul, extadd, conversions, dot, q15mul) — a real ~15-family breakdown, and works family-by-family.

Uses specific spec_json files as per-family checkpoints (simd_const.json 240→438/445), then plans to add per-shape arithmetic and conversion/narrowing families next — matching spec test as a rough done-check.

Milestone progress tracked mainly via aggregate score deltas and a handful of named json checks (i32.json, simd_shift, store8_lane) rather than an explicit per-family pass target; done-checks are ad-hoc, not a maintained living plan.

Ordered const/load/store/lane infrastructure before arithmetic that depends on it (fixed exec_numeric and v128 accessors first), showing dependency-aware sequencing, though the plan lines are repetitive and much 'planning' is compilation firefighting, not milestone structuring.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced MVP before/with SIMD and decomposed SIMD into its full ~15-family surface, implementing family-by-family with matching spec_json files (simd_const, simd_shift, store lane, i32) as rough checkpoints and some genuine dependency ordering (value type/const/load/lane infra before arithmetic) — solidly above the level-5 anchor. But it fell short of level 8: families were not each bound to a specific spec_json with an explicit pass target, no living/maintained milestone hierarchy existed (no TodoWrite, repetitive plan restatements), and progress was tracked mostly via aggregate score deltas amid heavy build-error firefighting. That places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification

evidence.note: Established baselines by running individual family jsons (i32, block, simd_const) and the full runner before/after early changes, reading concrete pass counts (240/445, 66/222) rather than a single final number.

Per-family loop: ran simd_const/simd_shift/simd_store, read FAIL and LEB-overflow errors, used wasm-objdump to verify actual opcode bytes (fd 0c), distinguishing an encoding mismatch from a logic bug; confirmed the fix by re-running (simd_const 240→438).
Traced store-lane 'no current module' and 'non-constant expr V128Const' FAIL reasons to specific validator/stack-order causes, then fixed and rebuilt — localized failures rather than guessing.

Diagnosed a runtime panic (empty mem_addrs at line 965) that was zeroing whole test files, and identified semantic bugs like i8x16 'halving instead of saturating' and an over-permissive assert_invalid validator by reading per-family output.
Repeatedly re-ran i32.json (MVP) alongside SIMD jsons and the full runner (score tracked 0.244→0.45→0.61), treating the aggregate as a monitored signal and guarding MVP against regressions.
Ended by declaring the task complete at score ~0.45 while summarizing 'most SIMD operations implemented' — the relentless pursuit of exact 1.0 lapsed, keeping this below the top anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran the systematic implement→run family json→read specific FAIL/error reasons→fix→re-run loop, periodically ran the full runner to track the aggregate score, and repeatedly re-checked MVP (i32.json) to guard against regressions — squarely the level-8 pattern. It also showed several level-10 traits: distinguishing an encoding mismatch (wrong 0xFD sub-opcodes, verified via wasm-objdump) from genuine semantic bugs (saturation, validator permissiveness, panics). It falls short of 10 because at the end it declared the task complete at ~0.45 rather than treating the aggregate as a signal to relentlessly drive toward the exact 1.0 target.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface

evidence.note: Tracks aggregate score (0.244→0.252) and per-file counts ('simd_const 240/445 → 438/445'), building a running numbered list of remaining issue families — clearly above a mere mental sense of progress.

Re-discovers the exact same exec_store pop-order 'critical bug' multiple times and flip-flops the change repeatedly across ~70 steps — thrashing not caught early, the failure mode the high anchors warn against.

Detects the shifting total-assertion denominator (33503→12696→33503) and correctly attributes it to silently-panicking modules, then re-reads the 'real picture' at 0.45 — genuine reconciliation of aggregate vs. per-family reality.

Maintains categorized remaining-work ledgers (validate_module/assert_invalid, missing SIMD ops, arithmetic bugs, shift) and quantifies the concrete gap to 1.0, but submits at 0.45 accurately reporting the shortfall rather than declaring false victory.
Score regresses 0.71→0.61→0.45 with the agent not fully reconciling whether the swing was denominator artifact or real regression — noisy aggregate tracking that keeps it below level 8.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent continuously quantifies both the aggregate score and per-family pass counts, keeps categorized remaining-work ledgers, and even catches the misleading denominator caused by panics — behavior well beyond the level-5 checklist anchor and reaching toward 8. But it fails the level-8 bar for detecting thrashing: it re-derives and flip-flops the identical exec_store pop-order bug several times over a long span, and its end-stage aggregate reconciliation (0.71→0.61→0.45) is noisy. That mix of solid quantified tracking with un-caught circular debugging places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Full runtime.rs rewrite caused 21 compile errors; agent recognized the approach was structurally wrong, reverted to backups, and switched to surgical incremental additions — a decisive course-correction on a falsified assumption.

Realized ALL SIMD sub-opcode numbers were wrong (sequential assumption falsified); used wasm-objdump to empirically derive the correct table and regenerated decode_simd once — fixing the generator so ~200 assertions flipped (simd_const 240→438). Level-8 behavior.

exec_store / lane pop-order assumption toggled back and forth repeatedly (addr-first vs val-first) across many steps — circular re-debugging of a single assumption rather than resolving the root cause once, which the top anchor explicitly warns against.

Late addition of validate_module regressed score from 0.638 to 0.45; agent submitted without detecting it broke previously-green families — failing the 'without breaking green families' clean-rework criterion.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly clears the level-5 anchor (steps back and reconsiders assumptions when a family stubbornly fails) and reaches level-8 at two points: the rewrite→surgical pivot (step 72) and especially the empirical opcode-table regeneration (steps 104-108), which fixed the generator of failures once and flipped many assertions together. However, it falls short of 8-10 overall because the store/lane pop-order assumption thrashed repeatedly (circular re-debugging), and its late validate_module change regressed the score without detection — violating the clean, non-regressing rework the higher anchors require. This places it at a 7: strong structural course-correction with residual circular re-debugging.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon systems task: understand an existing partial Rust WASM interpreter, fix its bugs/unimplemented MVP functions, then add the entire 128-bit SIMD proposal — hundreds of opcodes across ~15 semantic families (memory, splat, lane, bitwise, int/float arith, saturating, widen/narrow, conversions, dot, q15). Difficulty comes from breadth (must not lose track), subtle exact semantics (saturation, NaN, rounding, lane order), a hard fixed-interface constraint, and an all-or-nothing 1.0 target measured by a provided per-assertion spec-test harness. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, family-level decomposition, and tight incremental verification.

dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the provided skeleton (Value model, decode/runtime/types, which functions are stubbed or buggy, the fixed public contract) and the SIMD binary encoding + lane semantics before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task forbids rewriting and forbids touching spec.rs/main.rs or renaming public items; wrong assumptions about the existing Value representation or the 0xFD encoding propagate into every one of hundreds of opcodes. Getting exact per-family semantics (lane order, sat, NaN) is a research act, not guesswork.

anchors.0: Starts editing/adding opcodes without reading the existing sources or the spec-test format; invents an interface.
anchors.3: Skims one or two files; knows it's a WASM interpreter but not which functions are stubbed vs buggy, nor how v128 must slot into the existing Value type.
anchors.5: Reads decode.rs/runtime.rs/types.rs and identifies the public items that must not change, the existing value/stack model, and roughly how the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode is decoded; consults spec semantics for the common families.
anchors.8: Builds an explicit map of the codebase: what compiles, which MVP functions are unimplemented/buggy, exactly where value types, decoding, memory, and execution are wired, and how v128 must integrate without breaking the frozen interface. Pins down non-obvious semantics (saturation, NaN propagation, signed/unsigned lanes, extend low/high ordering) from the spec rather than guessing.
anchors.10: All of the above plus sustained, targeted re-research when a family behaves unexpectedly: probes specific spec-test cases to disambiguate encoding/rounding/lane-order questions, verifies the fixed public API surface concretely, and confirms encoding assumptions against wabt-generated output — orientation continually deepens as unfamiliar families are reached.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — first MVP correctness, then SIMD by instruction family — each milestone tied to a concrete spec-test json as its done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are hundreds of opcodes but a clean natural structure (MVP first; then per-family, each with its own spec_json file). Treating it as one undifferentiated push guarantees losing the plot and thrashing across unrelated failures.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random opcodes with no ordering or notion of completion.
anchors.3: Vague two-phase idea ('do MVP then SIMD') with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria.
anchors.5: Sequences MVP before SIMD and groups SIMD into a handful of families, implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 families with sensible dependency ordering (e.g. v128 value type + const/load/store and lane infra before arithmetic that depends on them), each milestone bound to a specific spec_json and a pass target, adjusted as families reveal shared infrastructure.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy: shared primitives (lane read/write, splat, per-shape iteration helpers) are sequenced first to avoid rework, families ordered by leverage, each with an explicit exit check, and the structure is revised as reality shifts scope — never a flat undifferentiated list, never redundant re-implementation across families.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided spec-test harness at fine granularity — per-family json files and the aggregate runner — to localize failures and confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1.0 (all-assertions) target is unforgiving; the harness reports per-assertion pass/fail per file, so a strategy of running individual family jsons and reading FAIL lines is the difference between fast localization and blind flailing across a giant surface.

anchors.0: Never builds/runs the tests, or only at the very end; declares done without evidence.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads only the final pass rate, without isolating which assertions fail or why.
anchors.5: Builds and runs the relevant per-family spec-test json after implementing each family, and uses FAIL lines to fix that family before moving on.
anchors.8: Systematic loop: implement family → run its json → read specific FAIL @ line reasons → fix → re-run to green, and periodically runs the full runner to confirm no regressions, keeping MVP files passing while adding SIMD.
anchors.10: Verification is engineered: drills into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (NaN, saturation boundaries, sign, lane order), distinguishes genuine bugs from encoding mismatches, guards against MVP regressions on every integration, and treats the aggregate score as a monitored signal rather than a one-shot final check — pursuing the exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing'.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which families/opcodes are done, which remain, and which are stuck, across a very long implementation horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of opcodes and a strict 1.0 bar, an agent that loses track will either declare victory with families unimplemented or re-debug the same failing case in circles.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs remaining; forgets whole families or repeats work.
anchors.3: Rough mental sense of progress; frequently surprised by unimplemented opcodes or unnoticed regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of families and current pass counts, updating it as families complete, and generally knows what remains.
anchors.8: Continuously reconciles per-family pass counts and the aggregate score against the full opcode list, notices when a fix in one family breaks another, and detects when it is stuck on a single assertion rather than making progress.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise done/remaining/blocked ledger over the whole surface, catches thrashing early (same FAIL recurring), quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely, and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining-assertion families instead of polishing already-green ones — the plot is never lost across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality diverges — e.g. a Value-type representation, decoding assumption, or semantic reading turns out wrong — rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (how v128 is stored, how lanes are read, how memory ops share code) and semantic guesses (sat/NaN/lane order) are easy to get subtly wrong; the fixed-interface constraint can also force a rethink. Detecting and reworking these beats piling fixes on a broken foundation.

anchors.0: Keeps applying local patches to a broken assumption; never revisits the root cause even as failures persist.
anchors.3: Occasionally tweaks approach under pressure but mostly forces the original plan regardless of evidence.
anchors.5: When a family stubbornly fails, steps back and reconsiders the relevant assumption (encoding, representation, or semantics) and adjusts.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a structural problem (e.g. shared lane/decoding helper is wrong, or a value-representation choice can't satisfy the frozen interface) and refactors the shared cause once, so many downstream assertions flip together.
anchors.10: Proactively distinguishes root-cause divergence from surface bugs, reworks the foundation decisively and cleanly without breaking green families, and updates its plan/milestones to reflect the new understanding — demonstrably avoiding circular re-debugging by fixing the generator of failures rather than each instance.
